requested_parts: The first Character dies while the ship's Pods are Locked. What happens to every Pod immediately
and can they subsequently be Locked again
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Starting it places a Status marker on the first (green) space of the Self-Destruct Track; the marker advances 1 space every time the Time marker advances. Any Character stopping the sequence removes the marker (a new sequence restarts from green). - At the **first yellow** space: the sequence can no longer be aborted, and all Escape Pods unlock instantly. They can be re-Locked; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again (FAQ Rules 25). - On the final ("skull") space: the ship explodes. - Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the **Coolant Leak Event can** start it despite sleepers (FAQ Rules 14). If a hyperspace jump happens while Self-Destruct is active, the ship is still considered destroyed. - **First Encounter:** the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this. - **First dead Character:** all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked (flip tokens). For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally (e.g., via the Hatch Control System). The first dead player may optionally continue as the Intruder player. - **Hibernation opens:** Characters CANNOT hibernate until the Time marker reaches any **blue** space of the Time Track. - **Self-Destruct point of no return:** when the Self-Destruct marker first reaches a **yellow** space, all Escape Pods unlock automatically (they can be Locked again; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again) and the sequence can no longer be stopped. - **The Time marker reaches the final red space of the Time Track** — the ship jumps to hyperspace immediately; every Character on board who is not hibernating dies from g-force. Intruders are unharmed by the hyperjump (so objectives like killing the Queen/a Breeder or destroying the Nest fail if not already done). - **The Self-Destruct marker reaches the final red ("skull") space of its Track, OR you are instructed to place a 9th Fire marker, OR a 9th Malfunction marker** — the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders (relevant to some Objectives). - **The last alive, non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates, or launches in an Escape Pod.** Then: if the Self-Destruct sequence was active, move its marker to its final red space; if not, move the Time marker to its final red space — and resolve those effects as above.

requested_parts: What does the Storage Room's Search for an Item Room Action let you draw and keep
where exactly does the rejected card go
and what are the common Room Action cost and restrictions
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Storage's Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero, paying the normal cost and obeying normal Room restrictions. Its counter limits only the Search Action card (Rooms 6). - Intranet research still requires the **Object itself in the Laboratory**, regardless of Scientist's location. Research means Analyse; the Object is retained, including for Objectives (Rooms 3–4). - Throwing a Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room makes you roll Noise in **your own Room**, not the Nest. An Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore the Nest's Egg total/hit points (Rooms 2, 9). - Smoke Grenade's affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their hand (Items 1). Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters (Items 2). - Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character's Weapon: trade them the Charge so they use it in their own round. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo. A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts **fully loaded**, rather than the one Ammo of a searched Weapon (Items 3, 5–6). - Alcohol's Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card (Items 4). - **Antidote:** scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from the game **and remove a Larva from your Character board, if present** (illustrated Antidote card, manual p.23). Gain 1 new Contamination card, and reshuffle that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in your hand. Then pass; you may keep hand cards. Surgery also removes a Larva, but shuffles the entire hand too, gives no new Contamination card and costs 1 Light Wound (Items 9; Rooms 1). - **Armory** — add 2 Ammo to 1 of your Energy Weapons (never Classic Weapons; never above capacity). - **Comms Room** — Send a Signal: place a Status marker on your board's Signal space (only used for Objectives). - **Emergency Room** — Dress ALL your Serious Wounds OR Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound OR Heal all your Light Wounds. - **Evacuation Section A / B** — try to enter an Unlocked Escape Pod with space in that Section: make a Noise roll; if any Intruder appears (or is present) in this Room, the attempt fails; otherwise board the Pod (2 spaces per Pod). - **Fire Control System** — choose any 1 Room: discard its Fire marker (if any) and ALL Intruders there run away in random directions (draw 1 Event card per Intruder). Works even with no Fire, to scatter Intruders. - **Generator** — initiate (or stop) the Self-Destruct sequence (Characters cannot start it while anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak Event is an exception). - **Laboratory** — Analyse 1 Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg present in the Room): reveal the corresponding Weakness card face up and leave it on the Intruder board. Its rule benefits all players. The Object is not consumed. - **Nest** — take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board, then make a Noise roll. No Search Action here. - **Storage** — draw 2 cards from a chosen Item deck (Red/Yellow/Green), keep 1, other to the bottom of that deck. - **Surgery** — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. requested_parts: You perform the Action printed on a One Use Only Item. Besides paying its Action-card cost and showing it
what happens to the Item card after use
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: These selected examples come from the original manual's card illustrations (pp.13,22–23). **One Use Only means discard that Item after its effect, in addition to paying its Action-card cost.** The table states the cost, consumption and Combat restriction together for each Item. Choose only one effect when a card gives alternatives. - Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2). - Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Actions 3; Items 10). The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost **because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action**. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7). - **Covering Fire:** Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7). - **Full Auto:** remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8). - **Nerves of Steel:** you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10). - Captain cannot use **Order** while personally in Combat. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape. **Motivation with Intercom** affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room (Actions 12–13). - Entering via **Technical Corridors** Action or **Technical Corridor Plans** ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined (Actions 14). - **Rest** with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19). - Basic Action: discard 1 Action card (Careful Movement: 2). - Action card: discard the card + its printed cost in extra cards. - Craft Item: **1 Action card + 2 matching Item cards**; discard the components and take the available Crafted card. - Room Action: discard 2 Action cards **while in that Room**, out of Combat and without a Malfunction there (unless an explicit special ability overrides location). - Item Action: discard the printed number of cards ("One Use Only" Items are also discarded). - Contamination cards can never pay costs.

requested_parts: For a rule concerned with the Character's arrival on Earth
where is a Character in a launched Escape Pod treated as having arrived
Does this establish that the ship itself reached Earth
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Regardless of Objective, **your Character must survive** (Escape Pod or hibernation). - *"Player X's Character cannot survive"* — that Character must simply be dead at game's end (not hibernated, not escaped); you don't have to kill them with your own Actions. - *"Your Character is the only survivor"* — no other Character may survive. - *"Send the Signal"* — perform the Comms Room Action (a Comms Room is always aboard). - *"The ship must reach Earth/Mars"* — the right Coordinates must be set in the Cockpit AND at least 2 of the 3 Engines must be Working. - *"Discover a Weakness"* — a corresponding Object must be researched in the Laboratory by anyone before game end. - *"Destroy the Nest"* — no Intruder Eggs may remain in it. - Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor. Effects of moving through a Corridor are resolved AFTER moving into the Room. - Two Rooms are **neighboring** when directly connected by 1 Corridor. A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement. - **After entering a Room:** (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. **A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.** Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise. Movement abilities that replace or cancel Noise retain their stated overrides. - To leave a Room containing an Intruder you must use the **Escape** rule (see Special Rules). - In the **Room Covered With Slime**, gain Slime immediately on entry, **before resolving its Exploration token**. A Silence Exploration token therefore resolves as Danger. - During Movement, Special Rooms are treated as already-explored Rooms. 1. **Engines**, only if the ship has survived: reveal all three top Engine tokens. **2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies**, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Launched Pod passengers are already away. A Room Malfunction never changes a Working Engine's token status. 2. **Coordinates**, only if the ship has survived: reveal the Coordinates card and read the destination selected by the Destination marker. **Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters**, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the **Quarantine Objective** survives if the destination is Mars. 3. **Contamination**, for **every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers**: - **No Larva already on board:** Scan every Contamination card from **Action deck, hand and discard pile**. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw. - **At least one Infected card, OR a Larva already on board:** shuffle **all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard** into a single new Action deck and draw the **top 4 cards**. **Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not; four Action cards with no Contamination means you survive this check.** A Larva skips the initial Scan but still requires this complete shuffle, draw and result check. - This endgame procedure does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected. 4. **Objectives:** each still-living Character reveals their chosen Objective and wins only if all requirements are fulfilled. Merely surviving is insufficient.

answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Unlock:** all Pods begin Locked. Unlock manually through Items/Hatch Control, or automatically on the first Character death or Self-Destruct's first yellow space. - **Board:** pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. - **Capacity:** 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. - **Launch immediately:** after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. - **Wait after boarding:** you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1). - **At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase**, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2). - **A second Character boards your waiting Pod:** the **new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants aboard**. Waiting by the first occupant does not prevent this launch or reserve launch control for them. - **An Intruder appears in the Section while you wait:** all Characters in that Section's Pods immediately return to its Room. - **A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait:** you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods (FAQ Rules 3). The original English manual and supplemental sources do not fully resolve these cases: all 8 Adult models in Combat when another must appear; whether a destroyed Nest is restored when Queen development adds an Egg; how to execute the missed Egg Melee Contamination waiver alongside the normal pre-roll draw; and whether later deaths re-unlock Pods after the first death’s unlock was reversed. The critical-moment rule says **first** death, while the English Escape Pods section says **any** death. The original French/German Pod sections say first death consistently, but are not identified as errata overriding the inconsistent English text. These remaining cases need an original-game publisher clarification or matching official erratum; no ruling is invented here. - **Encounter:** clear all connected Noise (including Technical Corridors if connected), draw a bag token, place its matching Intruder, compare its number to all cards in the triggering hand (including Contamination): fewer means Surprise Attack. **Keep the drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag** until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. A Blank instead restores connected Noise and returns to the bag. - **Shoot (1):** pick Weapon + target, discard 1 Ammo, roll Combat die; on a hit, add Injury marker(s), then draw an Intruder Attack card and check the Injury Effect (blood icon vs. Injury markers). - **Melee (1):** draw 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, pick a target in your Room, roll (2 Hits count as 1); on a miss you take 1 Serious Wound. Successful Egg Melee retains the normal Contamination draw; a missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound, with its draw timing unresolved (see Eggs). - **Escape (special Move, 1):** choose a neighboring Room; resolve 1 Intruder Attack per Intruder present; survive → move (explore/Noise roll as usual); die → Corpse stays behind. - **Intruder Attack:** target = Character with fewest Action cards in hand; draw 1 Attack card — matching Intruder symbol = hit (resolve effect), otherwise miss. - Intruder kill check: Larva/Egg die at 1 Injury; Creeper/Adult draw 1 card (blood ≤ Injuries = dead); Breeder/Queen draw 2 and add. answers.answer:
1. The summary states: **Intruder Attack** (happens on a Surprise Attack, in the Event Phase's Intruder Attack step, and on a Character's Escape): 1. Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order). A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper. 2. **Larva exception: draw no Attack card; use Infest below.** For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. Discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile; if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck. 4. **Time Track** — move the Time marker 1 space right. If the Self-Destruct Sequence is active, also move the Self-Destruct marker 1 space right. 5. **Intruder Attack** — each Intruder in Combat with a Character attacks them. 6. **Fire Damage** — each Intruder in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Injury. Apply Injury markers and the normal Injury Effect check immediately (including possible death or retreat). This happens after Intruder Attacks and before the Event card. 7. **Resolve 1 Event card**: - *Intruder movement:* all Intruders showing the card's Intruder symbol that are NOT in a Room with any Characters move to a neighboring Room through the Corridor matching the number on the card. An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7). - **Breeder** — all players roll for Noise in order (skip players in Combat), then return the Breeder token to the bag. - **Queen** — if any Characters are in the Nest Room, place the Queen miniature there and resolve an Encounter. If no Characters are in the Nest (or it hasn't been discovered), add 1 Egg token to the Intruder board. Return the token to the bag. - **Blank** — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag. 9. **End of the turn** — a new turn starts. requested_parts: An Event instructs removing itself from the game but its other effect cannot be resolved. Is it removed
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). **Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.** Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17). - Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6). Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). - Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23). On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24). - **Fire markers:** (1) a Character ending their round in a burning Room suffers 1 Light Wound (see Turn Structure); (2) each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check; (3) there are only 8 Fire markers — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship explodes and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool. Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms. Some Events spread Fire or add Malfunctions to burning Rooms. - **Malfunction markers:** (1) the Room's Action is unavailable (Searching still works); repair effects (Repair Action cards, Tools Item) can discard the marker; (2) only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room. Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime. They disable Special Rooms too (a Malfunction in the Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters; Engine status is never affected, only the Room Action). A Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22). - **Door tokens:** live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. **Open** = no token (all Doors start Open). **Closed** = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). **Destroyed** = lying token: movement allowed; **only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door**. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door. - **Slime marker:** while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. - **Noise markers:** only mark Corridors for the Noise roll rule; a marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor (never just one side of the Door). - When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it **on top of their Action discard pile**. It then cycles into their deck and hand like an Action card, but grants no Actions and cannot pay Action costs. - Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner: place the Scanner's red foil over the card's coded text field. If the exact word **INFECTED** appears in one line, the card is Infected; if it does not, the card is **not Infected**. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count. Unscanned cards remain unknown until the end of the game and can lose you the game at the Contamination check. - Scanning happens via specific effects (e.g., Rest Action card, Canteen/Shower/Surgery Room Actions, the Antidote Item; some Event cards also force Scans); each effect describes its own procedure. - **If an ordinary Scan shows INFECTED (follow its specific Action procedure; Surgery removes Infected cards/Larva, while Rest and Alcohol have the FAQ exceptions below):** place a Larva miniature on your Character board and do NOT remove that Contamination card. **If a Larva is already on your board, your Character dies — and place 1 Creeper in the Room where you died.** - When a rule removes a Contamination card, remove it from the game.

requested_parts: Does the Hand Serious Wound increase the cost of Basic Shoot, and why
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2). - Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Actions 3; Items 10). The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost **because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action**. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7). - **Covering Fire:** Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7). - **Full Auto:** remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8). - **Nerves of Steel:** you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10). - Captain cannot use **Order** while personally in Combat. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape. **Motivation with Intercom** affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room (Actions 12–13). - Entering via **Technical Corridors** Action or **Technical Corridor Plans** ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined (Actions 14). - **Rest** with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19). - Hand refills to 5 Action cards each turn (6 via Cabins). - 2 Actions per round; Room Actions cost 2 cards; Careful Movement 2; most everything else 1. - Intruder bag starts with: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults + 1 Adult per player. - Escape Pods: 2 (1–2 players) / 3 (3–4) / 4 (5 players); 2 Character spaces each. - 5 Eggs start on the Intruder board; 3 face-down Weakness cards (Corpse / Egg / Carcass). - 8 Fire markers, 8 Malfunction markers — a 9th of either ends the game with everyone still aboard dead; launched Pod passengers remain eligible for the Victory Check. - 2 of 3 Engines must be Working for a safe jump. - 3 Serious Wounds + any further Wound kills a Character; 3 Light Wounds convert to a Serious Wound. - Victory Check order: Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. - **Encounter:** clear all connected Noise (including Technical Corridors if connected), draw a bag token, place its matching Intruder, compare its number to all cards in the triggering hand (including Contamination): fewer means Surprise Attack. **Keep the drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag** until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. A Blank instead restores connected Noise and returns to the bag. - **Shoot (1):** pick Weapon + target, discard 1 Ammo, roll Combat die; on a hit, add Injury marker(s), then draw an Intruder Attack card and check the Injury Effect (blood icon vs. Injury markers). - **Melee (1):** draw 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, pick a target in your Room, roll (2 Hits count as 1); on a miss you take 1 Serious Wound. Successful Egg Melee retains the normal Contamination draw; a missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound, with its draw timing unresolved (see Eggs). - **Escape (special Move, 1):** choose a neighboring Room; resolve 1 Intruder Attack per Intruder present; survive → move (explore/Noise roll as usual); die → Corpse stays behind. - **Intruder Attack:** target = Character with fewest Action cards in hand; draw 1 Attack card — matching Intruder symbol = hit (resolve effect), otherwise miss. - Intruder kill check: Larva/Egg die at 1 Injury; Creeper/Adult draw 1 card (blood ≤ Injuries = dead); Breeder/Queen draw 2 and add. Retreat arrow on a drawn card = Intruder flees via an Event card's Corridor number.

requested_parts: A Larva attacks a Character who already has a Larva on their board. What happens to each Larva and to the Character
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it **on top of their Action discard pile**. It then cycles into their deck and hand like an Action card, but grants no Actions and cannot pay Action costs. - Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner: place the Scanner's red foil over the card's coded text field. If the exact word **INFECTED** appears in one line, the card is Infected; if it does not, the card is **not Infected**. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count. Unscanned cards remain unknown until the end of the game and can lose you the game at the Contamination check. - Scanning happens via specific effects (e.g., Rest Action card, Canteen/Shower/Surgery Room Actions, the Antidote Item; some Event cards also force Scans); each effect describes its own procedure. - **If an ordinary Scan shows INFECTED (follow its specific Action procedure; Surgery removes Infected cards/Larva, while Rest and Alcohol have the FAQ exceptions below):** place a Larva miniature on your Character board and do NOT remove that Contamination card. **If a Larva is already on your board, your Character dies — and place 1 Creeper in the Room where you died.** - When a rule removes a Contamination card, remove it from the game. 4. **Time Track** — move the Time marker 1 space right. If the Self-Destruct Sequence is active, also move the Self-Destruct marker 1 space right. 5. **Intruder Attack** — each Intruder in Combat with a Character attacks them. 6. **Fire Damage** — each Intruder in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Injury. Apply Injury markers and the normal Injury Effect check immediately (including possible death or retreat). This happens after Intruder Attacks and before the Event card. 7. **Resolve 1 Event card**: - *Intruder movement:* all Intruders showing the card's Intruder symbol that are NOT in a Room with any Characters move to a neighboring Room through the Corridor matching the number on the card. If the number indicates a Technical Corridor, remove that Intruder's miniature from the board and put its token back in the Intruder bag. - *Event effect:* after the movement step, resolve the effect described on the card. - Then discard the Event card (unless the card says otherwise). If the Event deck ever runs out (rare), shuffle the Event discards into a new deck. 8. **Intruder bag development** — draw 1 Intruder token from the bag: - **Larva** — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Adult token to the bag. - **Creeper** — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Breeder token to the bag. - **Adult** — return the token to the bag **immediately before** all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat). An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7). - **Breeder** — all players roll for Noise in order (skip players in Combat), then return the Breeder token to the bag. - **Queen** — if any Characters are in the Nest Room, place the Queen miniature there and resolve an Encounter. If no Characters are in the Nest (or it hasn't been discovered), add 1 Egg token to the Intruder board. Return the token to the bag. - **Blank** — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag. 9. **End of the turn** — a new turn starts. The turn only ends once the bag development step is fully resolved (all Encounters, Surprise Attacks, etc. played out). | Scan result | Card destination | Character outcome | |---|---|---| | Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result | | Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board | | Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place **1 Creeper** in the death Room |

To take a third, Drop one first. "Add"-type Items (Extended Magazine, Autoloader) attach to another card and act as one. **Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Item cards into one unit occupying 1 Hand slot**; it cannot combine Heavy Objects. - **Weapon Ammo:** a **Weapon found by Searching** starts with **1 Ammo**. This Ammo instruction applies to Weapons, rather than to every Heavy Item. A Weapon can never exceed its printed Ammo capacity. Starting and Crafted Weapons use their own loading rules. - **Heavy Objects:** Intruder Egg (mostly found in the Nest), Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass tokens — carried in Hand slots, needed for Laboratory research; no rules of their own. - **Drop:** free, any time during your turn, no Action. Dropped Objects stay in the Room; dropped Items are lost (discarded). - **Search eligibility:** the five printed **Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit and Engines 1–3 — cannot be Searched**. The **Nest and Room Covered With Slime also prohibit any Search Action**, although they are Room tiles rather than those five printed Special Rooms. In other Rooms, each Search lowers the Item Counter by 1; at 0 the Room cannot be searched (exception: Scout's Scavenging). Fire and Malfunction do not by themselves block Searching; the Search card's requirements still apply. Storage's Room Action is separate and can work at counter 0. - **Search procedure:** Red (Military), Yellow (Technical) and Green (Medical) Items can be found via the Search Action card; Blue Items are Crafted and never found by Searching. Match the Room's color (background under its name); in a **white** Room, choose any of the 3 decks. Draw **2 cards from that one deck → keep 1 → return the other face down to the bottom of that deck**, without shuffling (FAQ Actions 6). - **Crafting:** you may look through the Craft deck at any time. To Craft, pay **1 Action card plus 2 matching Item components**; discard those Items and take the available Crafted Item whose gray icons match their blue icons. The four Crafted Items and their component symbols (manual page 23) are: **Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric.** These are component symbols: discard two Items showing the matching blue icons, rather than assuming a particular Item name. If the Crafted card is unavailable, it cannot be built. - **Unlock:** all Pods begin Locked. Unlock manually through Items/Hatch Control, or automatically on the first Character death or Self-Destruct's first yellow space. - **Board:** pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. - **Capacity:** 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. - **Launch immediately:** after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. - **Wait after boarding:** you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1). - **At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase**, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2). - **A second Character boards your waiting Pod:** the **new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants aboard**. Waiting by the first occupant does not prevent this launch or reserve launch control for them. - **An Intruder appears in the Section while you wait:** all Characters in that Section's Pods immediately return to its Room. - **A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait:** you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods (FAQ Rules 3).

requested_parts: Can the Coolant Leak Event start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates
and how does that differ from starting it as a Character
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Starting it places a Status marker on the first (green) space of the Self-Destruct Track; the marker advances 1 space every time the Time marker advances. Any Character stopping the sequence removes the marker (a new sequence restarts from green). - At the **first yellow** space: the sequence can no longer be aborted, and all Escape Pods unlock instantly. They can be re-Locked; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again (FAQ Rules 25). - On the final ("skull") space: the ship explodes. - Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the **Coolant Leak Event can** start it despite sleepers (FAQ Rules 14). If a hyperspace jump happens while Self-Destruct is active, the ship is still considered destroyed. - **Cockpit** — Check Coordinates (secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie; replace it and remember it) OR Set Destination (move the Destination marker). **The marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card:** read the entry corresponding to its track space when checking where the ship will jump. You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating. - **Engines #1–#3** — Check the Engine (secretly look at the TOP token; you may lie). Repair/Break Engine (via a Repairs Action or Tools Item): secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order — you needn't say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order. Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first. - **Hibernatorium** — Try to hibernate: pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing in the Room makes the attempt fail. Otherwise remove your miniature and stop participating until the end checks. **Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception.** A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers. - **Armory** — add 2 Ammo to 1 of your Energy Weapons (never Classic Weapons; never above capacity). - **Comms Room** — Send a Signal: place a Status marker on your board's Signal space (only used for Objectives). - **Emergency Room** — Dress ALL your Serious Wounds OR Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound OR Heal all your Light Wounds. - **Evacuation Section A / B** — try to enter an Unlocked Escape Pod with space in that Section: make a Noise roll; if any Intruder appears (or is present) in this Room, the attempt fails; otherwise board the Pod (2 spaces per Pod). - **Fire Control System** — choose any 1 Room: discard its Fire marker (if any) and ALL Intruders there run away in random directions (draw 1 Event card per Intruder). Works even with no Fire, to scatter Intruders. - **Generator** — initiate (or stop) the Self-Destruct sequence (Characters cannot start it while anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak Event is an exception). - **Laboratory** — Analyse 1 Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg present in the Room): reveal the corresponding Weakness card face up and leave it on the Intruder board. Its rule benefits all players. The Object is not consumed. - **Nest** — take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board, then make a Noise roll. No Search Action here. - **Storage** — draw 2 cards from a chosen Item deck (Red/Yellow/Green), keep 1, other to the bottom of that deck. - **Surgery** — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.

requested_parts: Where do discarded/dead Intruder tokens go
and can they be reused later
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). **Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.** Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17). - Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6). Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). - Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23). On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24). - **First Encounter:** the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this. - **First dead Character:** all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked (flip tokens). For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally (e.g., via the Hatch Control System). The first dead player may optionally continue as the Intruder player. - **Hibernation opens:** Characters CANNOT hibernate until the Time marker reaches any **blue** space of the Time Track. - **Self-Destruct point of no return:** when the Self-Destruct marker first reaches a **yellow** space, all Escape Pods unlock automatically (they can be Locked again; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again) and the sequence can no longer be stopped. **Routing rule:** Action and gained Contamination cards go to that Character's Action discard; Items go to the matching Item discard; Event, Intruder Attack and Serious Wound cards each go to their own discard. **Discarded markers return to their matching supply pools.** An explicit effect can give a different destination: Search and Storage keep one of two Item cards and return the other face down to the bottom of the chosen deck. Removed-from-game Contamination and Exploration tokens do not return to their supplies.

requested_parts: Can Fire and Malfunction markers be placed in unexplored Rooms
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - **Fire markers:** (1) a Character ending their round in a burning Room suffers 1 Light Wound (see Turn Structure); (2) each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check; (3) there are only 8 Fire markers — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship explodes and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool. Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms. Some Events spread Fire or add Malfunctions to burning Rooms. - **Malfunction markers:** (1) the Room's Action is unavailable (Searching still works); repair effects (Repair Action cards, Tools Item) can discard the marker; (2) only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room. Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime. They disable Special Rooms too (a Malfunction in the Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters; Engine status is never affected, only the Room Action). A Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22). - **Door tokens:** live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. **Open** = no token (all Doors start Open). **Closed** = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). **Destroyed** = lying token: movement allowed; **only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door**. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door. - **Slime marker:** while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. - **Noise markers:** only mark Corridors for the Noise roll rule; a marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor (never just one side of the Door). - **Airlock Control** — pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors: automatically Close every Door around it and place the Airlock Procedure token there. If all those Doors are still Closed when the current Player Phase ends (all players passed), EVERYTHING in that Room dies (Characters and Intruders) and any Fire marker there is removed; if any of the Doors is opened first, the procedure is cancelled. - **Cabins** — passive: at the start of a new turn, a Character here with no Intruders present draws 1 extra Action card (hand of 6 instead of 5). Disabled by a Malfunction token. - **Canteen** — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). - **Command Center** — choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which). - **Engine Control Room** — check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here). - **Hatch Control System** — flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. - **Monitoring Room** — secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw). - **Room Covered With Slime** — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker **before resolving its Exploration token**, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). - **Shower Room** — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering. **Special Rooms** (printed on the board, start explored, no Searching; Fire/Malfunction apply normally):

answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - Hand refills to 5 Action cards each turn (6 via Cabins). - 2 Actions per round; Room Actions cost 2 cards; Careful Movement 2; most everything else 1. - Intruder bag starts with: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults + 1 Adult per player. - Escape Pods: 2 (1–2 players) / 3 (3–4) / 4 (5 players); 2 Character spaces each. - 5 Eggs start on the Intruder board; 3 face-down Weakness cards (Corpse / Egg / Carcass). - 8 Fire markers, 8 Malfunction markers — a 9th of either ends the game with everyone still aboard dead; launched Pod passengers remain eligible for the Victory Check. - 2 of 3 Engines must be Working for a safe jump. - 3 Serious Wounds + any further Wound kills a Character; 3 Light Wounds convert to a Serious Wound. - Victory Check order: Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. | Item | Action-card cost and use | Combat restriction | Effect | |---|---|---|---| | Bandages | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | Out of Combat only | **Dress 1 Serious Wound OR Heal all Light Wounds.** Dressing does not Heal or discard a Serious Wound. | | Clothes | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | Out of Combat only | **Discard your Slime marker OR Dress 1 Serious Wound.** | | Fire Extinguisher | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | **Discard Fire from your current Room OR choose 1 Intruder in your current Room and force it to Retreat.** It does not combine both effects or affect all Intruders like Fire Control System. | | Taser | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | Choose **1 Intruder in your Room**: it suffers **1 Injury and Retreats**. OR choose **1 Character in your Room**: they discard **all cards in their hand**, including Contamination cards. | | Energy Charge | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | **Fully load 1 of your own Energy Weapons** (up to its Ammo capacity) OR **Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your Room**. The normal prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors applies. To reload someone else's Weapon, Trade the Charge to them first; you cannot use it directly on their Weapon. | | Molotov Cocktail | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | Choose your Room or a neighboring Room **containing an Intruder** (uncarried Eggs also permit the target, as under Eggs). **Place Fire** there; immediately, **each Intruder suffers 1 Injury and each Character suffers 1 Serious Wound**, including you if you are there. This immediate damage is separate from later Fire damage. | | Nemesis Plans | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | Out of Combat only | Privately check **any 2 unexplored Room tiles**, then return them face down. **Do not inspect their Exploration tokens**. Monitoring Room, by contrast, checks 1 tile together with its token. | - **Airlock Control** — pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors: automatically Close every Door around it and place the Airlock Procedure token there. If all those Doors are still Closed when the current Player Phase ends (all players passed), EVERYTHING in that Room dies (Characters and Intruders) and any Fire marker there is removed; if any of the Doors is opened first, the procedure is cancelled. - **Cabins** — passive: at the start of a new turn, a Character here with no Intruders present draws 1 extra Action card (hand of 6 instead of 5). Disabled by a Malfunction token. - **Canteen** — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). - **Command Center** — choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which). - **Engine Control Room** — check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here). - **Hatch Control System** — flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. - **Monitoring Room** — secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw). - **Room Covered With Slime** — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker **before resolving its Exploration token**, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). - **Shower Room** — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering.

requested_parts: On a Character death in standard play
what happens to Heavy Objects versus their Item cards
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). **Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.** Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17). - Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6). Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). - Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23). On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24). - **Unlock:** all Pods begin Locked. Unlock manually through Items/Hatch Control, or automatically on the first Character death or Self-Destruct's first yellow space. - **Board:** pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. - **Capacity:** 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. - **Launch immediately:** after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. - **Wait after boarding:** you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1). - **At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase**, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2). - **A second Character boards your waiting Pod:** the **new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants aboard**. Waiting by the first occupant does not prevent this launch or reserve launch control for them. - **An Intruder appears in the Section while you wait:** all Characters in that Section's Pods immediately return to its Room. - **A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait:** you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods (FAQ Rules 3). - **Light Wounds:** track on your Character board — 1st marker on the upper space, 2nd on the lower space (= 2 Light Wounds); on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a **Serious Wound**. - **Serious Wounds:** draw a Serious Wound card and place it by your board; its effect applies immediately. Duplicate Serious Wound cards are NOT cumulative (but are harder to get rid of). - **Death:** a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there. - **Dress a Serious Wound:** flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. **Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.** **Heal:** remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. (Sources include Clothes, Bandages, MedKit Items and the Emergency Room.)

requested_parts: Self-Destruct reaches its first yellow space, Pods unlock, then are relocked. Does reaching the next yellow space unlock them again
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - **First Encounter:** the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this. - **First dead Character:** all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked (flip tokens). For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally (e.g., via the Hatch Control System). The first dead player may optionally continue as the Intruder player. - **Hibernation opens:** Characters CANNOT hibernate until the Time marker reaches any **blue** space of the Time Track. - **Self-Destruct point of no return:** when the Self-Destruct marker first reaches a **yellow** space, all Escape Pods unlock automatically (they can be Locked again; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again) and the sequence can no longer be stopped. - **Unlock:** all Pods begin Locked. Unlock manually through Items/Hatch Control, or automatically on the first Character death or Self-Destruct's first yellow space. - **Board:** pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. - **Capacity:** 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. - **Launch immediately:** after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. - **Wait after boarding:** you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1). - **At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase**, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2). - **A second Character boards your waiting Pod:** the **new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants aboard**. Waiting by the first occupant does not prevent this launch or reserve launch control for them. - **An Intruder appears in the Section while you wait:** all Characters in that Section's Pods immediately return to its Room. - **A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait:** you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods (FAQ Rules 3). - Starting it places a Status marker on the first (green) space of the Self-Destruct Track; the marker advances 1 space every time the Time marker advances. Any Character stopping the sequence removes the marker (a new sequence restarts from green). - At the **first yellow** space: the sequence can no longer be aborted, and all Escape Pods unlock instantly. They can be re-Locked; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again (FAQ Rules 25). - On the final ("skull") space: the ship explodes. - Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the **Coolant Leak Event can** start it despite sleepers (FAQ Rules 14). If a hyperspace jump happens while Self-Destruct is active, the ship is still considered destroyed.

does that alone make your Character a winner
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). what if honest negotiations end without a trade
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost **because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action**. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7). - **Covering Fire:** Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7). - **Full Auto:** remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8). - **Nerves of Steel:** you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10). - Captain cannot use **Order** while personally in Combat. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape. **Motivation with Intercom** affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room (Actions 12–13). - Entering via **Technical Corridors** Action or **Technical Corridor Plans** ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined (Actions 14). - **Rest** with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19). 1. **Draw Action cards** — every player draws from their Action deck up to a hand of **5 cards**. Whenever you must draw and your Action deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck, then draw. 2. **First Player token** — after drawing, pass the token to the player on the left (do NOT pass it on the first turn of the game). Whenever players do anything "in order," start with the First Player and go clockwise. 3. **Player rounds** — starting with the First Player and going clockwise, each **active player who has not passed** performs a **round of 2 Actions**. Repeat rounds in that order, **skipping players who have passed for ordinary Actions**, while anyone remains active. **Only when everyone has passed does the Player Phase end and the Event Phase begin.** The Interruption exception below still applies. You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating. - **Engines #1–#3** — Check the Engine (secretly look at the TOP token; you may lie). Repair/Break Engine (via a Repairs Action or Tools Item): secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order — you needn't say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order. Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first. - **Hibernatorium** — Try to hibernate: pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing in the Room makes the attempt fail. Otherwise remove your miniature and stop participating until the end checks. **Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception.** A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.

requested_parts: Which Basic Actions can be used in Combat
can you Trade, Craft or Pick Up an Object there
What about permitted card or Item Actions
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: **Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape: no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation.** Room Actions remain forbidden (FAQ Actions 3–5). - **Movement** — move your miniature to a neighboring Room, applying all Movement rules (see below). - **Careful Movement** (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too. - **Shoot** (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo) — attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand, discarding 1 Ammo from that Weapon's card. - **Melee Attack** — attack an Intruder in your Room with bare hands or improvised means. - **Pick Up Heavy Object** (cost 1 Action card) — pick up 1 Heavy Object in your Room (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Intruder Egg) into a Hand slot. This Basic pickup has no Noise-roll instruction; taking an Egg still on the Intruder board instead uses the Nest Room Action, costs 2 cards and then rolls Noise. (Heavy Items found by Searching do not require this Action — it applies to Objects only.) - **Trade** — trade with all Characters in your Room. Players show each other any Item cards/Objects they wish; exchanges happen if both parties agree. Only the initiator spends the Action. You may give an Item/Object for nothing. **Characters cannot exchange Ammo.** - **Craft Item** — pay **1 Action card and discard 2 Item cards** showing the appropriate blue Craft (Component) icons to take the Crafted Item card showing those same icons in gray. A Crafted Item cannot be built if its card is not available, even with the right components. - Basic Action: discard 1 Action card (Careful Movement: 2). - Action card: discard the card + its printed cost in extra cards. - Craft Item: **1 Action card + 2 matching Item cards**; discard the components and take the available Crafted card. - Room Action: discard 2 Action cards **while in that Room**, out of Combat and without a Malfunction there (unless an explicit special ability overrides location). - Item Action: discard the printed number of cards ("One Use Only" Items are also discarded). - Contamination cards can never pay costs.

requested_parts: Can Soldier use Covering Fire only on themselves
and how are direction, Noise and Surprise targeting handled when moving two Characters
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2). - Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Actions 3; Items 10). The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost **because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action**. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7). - **Covering Fire:** Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7). - **Full Auto:** remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8). - **Nerves of Steel:** you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10). - Captain cannot use **Order** while personally in Combat. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape. **Motivation with Intercom** affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room (Actions 12–13). - Entering via **Technical Corridors** Action or **Technical Corridor Plans** ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined (Actions 14). - **Rest** with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19). - Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor. Effects of moving through a Corridor are resolved AFTER moving into the Room. - Two Rooms are **neighboring** when directly connected by 1 Corridor. requested_parts: Careful Movement or Reconnaissance reveals a Danger/Silence Exploration token. Does that automatic result apply or the movement ability
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor. Effects of moving through a Corridor are resolved AFTER moving into the Room. - Two Rooms are **neighboring** when directly connected by 1 Corridor. A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement. - **After entering a Room:** (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. **A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.** Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise. Movement abilities that replace or cancel Noise retain their stated overrides. - To leave a Room containing an Intruder you must use the **Escape** rule (see Special Rules). - In the **Room Covered With Slime**, gain Slime immediately on entry, **before resolving its Exploration token**. A Silence Exploration token therefore resolves as Danger. - During Movement, Special Rooms are treated as already-explored Rooms. - **Movement** — move your miniature to a neighboring Room, applying all Movement rules (see below). - **Careful Movement** (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too. - **Shoot** (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo) — attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand, discarding 1 Ammo from that Weapon's card. - **Melee Attack** — attack an Intruder in your Room with bare hands or improvised means. - **Pick Up Heavy Object** (cost 1 Action card) — pick up 1 Heavy Object in your Room (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Intruder Egg) into a Hand slot. This Basic pickup has no Noise-roll instruction; taking an Egg still on the Intruder board instead uses the Nest Room Action, costs 2 cards and then rolls Noise. (Heavy Items found by Searching do not require this Action — it applies to Objects only.) - **Trade** — trade with all Characters in your Room. Players show each other any Item cards/Objects they wish; exchanges happen if both parties agree. Only the initiator spends the Action. You may give an Item/Object for nothing. **Characters cannot exchange Ammo.** - **Craft Item** — pay **1 Action card and discard 2 Item cards** showing the appropriate blue Craft (Component) icons to take the Crafted Item card showing those same icons in gray. A Crafted Item cannot be built if its card is not available, even with the right components. - **Fire markers:** (1) a Character ending their round in a burning Room suffers 1 Light Wound (see Turn Structure); (2) each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check; (3) there are only 8 Fire markers — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship explodes and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool. Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms. Some Events spread Fire or add Malfunctions to burning Rooms. - **Malfunction markers:** (1) the Room's Action is unavailable (Searching still works); repair effects (Repair Action cards, Tools Item) can discard the marker; (2) only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room. Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime. They disable Special Rooms too (a Malfunction in the Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters; Engine status is never affected, only the Room Action). A Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22). - **Door tokens:** live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. **Open** = no token (all Doors start Open). **Closed** = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). **Destroyed** = lying token: movement allowed; **only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door**. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door. - **Slime marker:** while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. - **Noise markers:** only mark Corridors for the Noise roll rule; a marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor (never just one side of the Door).
