requested_parts: You throw a Grenade/Molotov at uncarried Eggs in the Nest from a neighboring Room. Where is the required Noise roll resolved
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - Storage's Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero, paying the normal cost and obeying normal Room restrictions. Its counter limits only the Search Action card (Rooms 6). - Intranet research still requires the **Object itself in the Laboratory**, regardless of Scientist's location. Research means Analyse; the Object is retained, including for Objectives (Rooms 3–4). - Throwing a Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room makes you roll Noise in **your own Room**, not the Nest. An Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore the Nest's Egg total/hit points (Rooms 2, 9). - Smoke Grenade's affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their hand (Items 1). Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters (Items 2). - Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character's Weapon: trade them the Charge so they use it in their own round. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo. A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts **fully loaded**, rather than the one Ammo of a searched Weapon (Items 3, 5–6). - Alcohol's Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card (Items 4). - **Antidote:** scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from the game **and remove a Larva from your Character board, if present** (illustrated Antidote card, manual p.23). Gain 1 new Contamination card, and reshuffle that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in your hand. Then pass; you may keep hand cards. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below. | | Grenade | Destroys **2 Eggs**. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. | | Molotov Cocktail | Destroys **1 Egg** immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. | | **Fire marker** | Normally destroys **1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step**. For the **Nest's Egg pool**, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to **2** per step (FAQ Rooms 7). | - **Egg Melee penalties:** a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of **1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile**. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified. - **Noise after an attack attempt:** after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).

requested_parts: When the Nest is on Fire and Vulnerability to Fire is discovered
how many of its Eggs are destroyed each Fire Damage step
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: | Method against uncarried Eggs | Egg destruction | |---|---| | Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys **1 Egg**. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below. | | Grenade | Destroys **2 Eggs**. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. | | Molotov Cocktail | Destroys **1 Egg** immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. | | **Fire marker** | Normally destroys **1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step**. For the **Nest's Egg pool**, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to **2** per step (FAQ Rooms 7). | - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). **Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.** Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17). - Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6). Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). - Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23). On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24). 4. **Time Track** — move the Time marker 1 space right. answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it **on top of their Action discard pile**. It then cycles into their deck and hand like an Action card, but grants no Actions and cannot pay Action costs. - Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner: place the Scanner's red foil over the card's coded text field. If the exact word **INFECTED** appears in one line, the card is Infected; if it does not, the card is **not Infected**. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count. Unscanned cards remain unknown until the end of the game and can lose you the game at the Contamination check. - Scanning happens via specific effects (e.g., Rest Action card, Canteen/Shower/Surgery Room Actions, the Antidote Item; some Event cards also force Scans); each effect describes its own procedure. - **If an ordinary Scan shows INFECTED (follow its specific Action procedure; Surgery removes Infected cards/Larva, while Rest and Alcohol have the FAQ exceptions below):** place a Larva miniature on your Character board and do NOT remove that Contamination card. **If a Larva is already on your board, your Character dies — and place 1 Creeper in the Room where you died.** - When a rule removes a Contamination card, remove it from the game. - Storage's Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero, paying the normal cost and obeying normal Room restrictions. Its counter limits only the Search Action card (Rooms 6). - Intranet research still requires the **Object itself in the Laboratory**, regardless of Scientist's location. Research means Analyse; the Object is retained, including for Objectives (Rooms 3–4). - Throwing a Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room makes you roll Noise in **your own Room**, not the Nest. An Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore the Nest's Egg total/hit points (Rooms 2, 9). - Smoke Grenade's affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their hand (Items 1). Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters (Items 2). - Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character's Weapon: trade them the Charge so they use it in their own round. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo. A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts **fully loaded**, rather than the one Ammo of a searched Weapon (Items 3, 5–6). - Alcohol's Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card (Items 4). - **Antidote:** scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from the game **and remove a Larva from your Character board, if present** (illustrated Antidote card, manual p.23). Disabled by a Malfunction token. - **Canteen** — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). - **Command Center** — choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which). - **Engine Control Room** — check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here). - **Hatch Control System** — flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. - **Monitoring Room** — secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw). - **Room Covered With Slime** — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker **before resolving its Exploration token**, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). - **Shower Room** — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering.

answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Fire markers:** (1) a Character ending their round in a burning Room suffers 1 Light Wound (see Turn Structure); (2) each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check; (3) there are only 8 Fire markers — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship explodes and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool. Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms. Some Events spread Fire or add Malfunctions to burning Rooms. - **Malfunction markers:** (1) the Room's Action is unavailable (Searching still works); repair effects (Repair Action cards, Tools Item) can discard the marker; (2) only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room. Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime. They disable Special Rooms too (a Malfunction in the Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters; Engine status is never affected, only the Room Action). A Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22). - **Door tokens:** live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. **Open** = no token (all Doors start Open). **Closed** = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). **Destroyed** = lying token: movement allowed; **only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door**. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door. - **Slime marker:** while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. - **Noise markers:** only mark Corridors for the Noise roll rule; a marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor (never just one side of the Door). 1. **Item Counter:** **the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count**. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot. 2. **Resolve the effect:** - **Silence — no Movement Noise roll.** Nothing happens. OR choose **1 Character in your Room**: they discard **all cards in their hand**, including Contamination cards. | | Energy Charge | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | **Fully load 1 of your own Energy Weapons** (up to its Ammo capacity) OR **Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your Room**. The normal prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors applies. requested_parts: During the Event Phase Fire Damage step
how many Injuries does each Intruder in a burning Room take
when relative to attacks
and does it trigger an Injury Effect check
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: 4. **Time Track** — move the Time marker 1 space right. If the Self-Destruct Sequence is active, also move the Self-Destruct marker 1 space right. 5. **Intruder Attack** — each Intruder in Combat with a Character attacks them. 6. **Fire Damage** — each Intruder in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Injury. Apply Injury markers and the normal Injury Effect check immediately (including possible death or retreat). This happens after Intruder Attacks and before the Event card. 7. **Resolve 1 Event card**: - *Intruder movement:* all Intruders showing the card's Intruder symbol that are NOT in a Room with any Characters move to a neighboring Room through the Corridor matching the number on the card. If the number indicates a Technical Corridor, remove that Intruder's miniature from the board and put its token back in the Intruder bag. - *Event effect:* after the movement step, resolve the effect described on the card. - Then discard the Event card (unless the card says otherwise). If the Event deck ever runs out (rare), shuffle the Event discards into a new deck. 8. **Intruder bag development** — draw 1 Intruder token from the bag: - **Larva** — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Adult token to the bag. - **Creeper** — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Breeder token to the bag. - **Adult** — return the token to the bag **immediately before** all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat). An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7). - **Breeder** — all players roll for Noise in order (skip players in Combat), then return the Breeder token to the bag. - **Queen** — if any Characters are in the Nest Room, place the Queen miniature there and resolve an Encounter. If no Characters are in the Nest (or it hasn't been discovered), add 1 Egg token to the Intruder board. Return the token to the bag. - **Blank** — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag. 9. **End of the turn** — a new turn starts. The turn only ends once the bag development step is fully resolved (all Encounters, Surprise Attacks, etc. played out). | Method against uncarried Eggs | Egg destruction | |---|---| | Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys **1 Egg**. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below. | | Grenade | Destroys **2 Eggs**. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. | | Molotov Cocktail | Destroys **1 Egg** immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. | | **Fire marker** | Normally destroys **1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step**. For the **Nest's Egg pool**, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to **2** per step (FAQ Rooms 7). | - **Empty-hand sequence:** completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does **not** automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). **Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.** Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17). - Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6). Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19). - A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With **The Way of Moving** Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8). - **Vulnerability to Fire** gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7). - A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13). Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). - Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23). requested_parts: Can you perform any Search Action in the Nest or Room Covered With Slime, even though ordinary Room tiles usually permit searching
answers.answer: 1. The summary states: - **Sources:** starting Weapon; 2 Quest Items (start horizontal/inactive — fulfill the condition on the card to flip them into normal Items); Searching; Crafting. - **Inventory (normal Items):** hidden in your card holder — others see only card backs/colors. No Inventory size limit. Any Item used must be shown to all players. - **Heavy Items and Objects (Hand icon):** never hidden; each occupies one of your **2 Hand slots**. To take a third, Drop one first. "Add"-type Items (Extended Magazine, Autoloader) attach to another card and act as one. **Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Item cards into one unit occupying 1 Hand slot**; it cannot combine Heavy Objects. - **Weapon Ammo:** a **Weapon found by Searching** starts with **1 Ammo**. This Ammo instruction applies to Weapons, rather than to every Heavy Item. A Weapon can never exceed its printed Ammo capacity. Starting and Crafted Weapons use their own loading rules. - **Heavy Objects:** Intruder Egg (mostly found in the Nest), Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass tokens — carried in Hand slots, needed for Laboratory research; no rules of their own. - **Drop:** free, any time during your turn, no Action. Dropped Objects stay in the Room; dropped Items are lost (discarded). - **Search eligibility:** the five printed **Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit and Engines 1–3 — cannot be Searched**. The **Nest and Room Covered With Slime also prohibit any Search Action**, although they are Room tiles rather than those five printed Special Rooms. In other Rooms, each Search lowers the Item Counter by 1; at 0 the Room cannot be searched (exception: Scout's Scavenging). Fire and Malfunction do not by themselves block Searching; the Search card's requirements still apply. Storage's Room Action is separate and can work at counter 0. - **Search procedure:** Red (Military), Yellow (Technical) and Green (Medical) Items can be found via the Search Action card; Blue Items are Crafted and never found by Searching. Match the Room's color (background under its name); in a **white** Room, choose any of the 3 decks. Draw **2 cards from that one deck → keep 1 → return the other face down to the bottom of that deck**, without shuffling (FAQ Actions 6). - **Crafting:** you may look through the Craft deck at any time. To Craft, pay **1 Action card plus 2 matching Item components**; discard those Items and take the available Crafted Item whose gray icons match their blue icons. The four Crafted Items and their component symbols (manual page 23) are: **Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric.** These are component symbols: discard two Items showing the matching blue icons, rather than assuming a particular Item name. If the Crafted card is unavailable, it cannot be built. - **Airlock Control** — pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors: automatically Close every Door around it and place the Airlock Procedure token there. If all those Doors are still Closed when the current Player Phase ends (all players passed), EVERYTHING in that Room dies (Characters and Intruders) and any Fire marker there is removed; if any of the Doors is opened first, the procedure is cancelled. - **Cabins** — passive: at the start of a new turn, a Character here with no Intruders present draws 1 extra Action card (hand of 6 instead of 5). Disabled by a Malfunction token. - **Canteen** — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). - **Command Center** — choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which). - **Engine Control Room** — check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here). - **Hatch Control System** — flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. - **Monitoring Room** — secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw). - **Room Covered With Slime** — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker **before resolving its Exploration token**, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). - **Shower Room** — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering. - **Fire markers:** (1) a Character ending their round in a burning Room suffers 1 Light Wound (see Turn Structure); (2) each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check; (3) there are only 8 Fire markers — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship explodes and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool. Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms. Some Events spread Fire or add Malfunctions to burning Rooms. - **Malfunction markers:** (1) the Room's Action is unavailable (Searching still works); repair effects (Repair Action cards, Tools Item) can discard the marker; (2) only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, **the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends**. Max 1 per Room. Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime. They disable Special Rooms too (a Malfunction in the Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters; Engine status is never affected, only the Room Action). A Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22). - **Door tokens:** live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. **Open** = no token (all Doors start Open). **Closed** = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). **Destroyed** = lying token: movement allowed; **only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door**. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door. - **Slime marker:** while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. - **Noise markers:** only mark Corridors for the Noise roll rule; a marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor (never just one side of the Door).

This Ammo instruction applies to Weapons, rather than to every Heavy Item. A Weapon can never exceed its printed Ammo capacity. Starting and Crafted Weapons use their own loading rules. - **Heavy Objects:** Intruder Egg (mostly found in the Nest), Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass tokens — carried in Hand slots, needed for Laboratory research; no rules of their own. - **Drop:** free, any time during your turn, no Action. requested_parts: What does the Six Shooter card require for reloading
and how many Injuries does its single-crosshair Combat die result deal when no Weakness changes damage
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: The illustrated **Six Shooter** is a Classic Weapon with Ammo capacity 6: it can only be reloaded with a **Reload Action card**, and a **single-crosshair** result deals **1 additional Injury** (2 total before other modifiers). The page-19 **Scientist's Pistol** treats a **two-crosshair** result as **only 1 Injury**, followed by the normal Injury Effect check. The illustrated **Flamethrower** is a Classic Weapon with Ammo capacity 4: when shooting it always deals at least **1 Injury except on the blank miss face**, even if the rolled Intruder symbol would normally miss that target. A **two-crosshair** result deals the normal 2 Injuries and also places a Fire marker in **your Room**. Apply normal Shoot costs, targeting and Injury Effect checks; marker limits still apply. **Melee Attack (cost 1):** (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die. Results mirror Shooting with two changes: **any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound on your Character**, and the 2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury (in melee, rolls of 2 Hits are treated as 1 Hit). - **Encounter:** clear all connected Noise (including Technical Corridors if connected), draw a bag token, place its matching Intruder, compare its number to all cards in the triggering hand (including Contamination): fewer means Surprise Attack. **Keep the drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag** until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. A Blank instead restores connected Noise and returns to the bag. - **Shoot (1):** pick Weapon + target, discard 1 Ammo, roll Combat die; on a hit, add Injury marker(s), then draw an Intruder Attack card and check the Injury Effect (blood icon vs. Injury markers). - **Melee (1):** draw 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, pick a target in your Room, roll (2 Hits count as 1); on a miss you take 1 Serious Wound. Successful Egg Melee retains the normal Contamination draw; a missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound, with its draw timing unresolved (see Eggs). - **Escape (special Move, 1):** choose a neighboring Room; resolve 1 Intruder Attack per Intruder present; survive → move (explore/Noise roll as usual); die → Corpse stays behind. - **Intruder Attack:** target = Character with fewest Action cards in hand; draw 1 Attack card — matching Intruder symbol = hit (resolve effect), otherwise miss. - Intruder kill check: Larva/Egg die at 1 Injury; Creeper/Adult draw 1 card (blood ≤ Injuries = dead); Breeder/Queen draw 2 and add. Retreat arrow on a drawn card = Intruder flees via an Event card's Corridor number.

requested_parts: The Captain plays Suppressive Fire, whose printed Action cost is 0. Must any Ammo still be spent
Does it move both the Captain and another Character, or one selected Character
must that other Character agree
and are the normal Escape attacks resolved
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2). - Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Actions 3; Items 10). The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost **because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action**. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7). - **Covering Fire:** Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7). - **Full Auto:** remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8). - **Nerves of Steel:** you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10). - Captain cannot use **Order** while personally in Combat. OR choose **1 Character in your Room**: they discard **all cards in their hand**, including Contamination cards. | | Energy Charge | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | **Fully load 1 of your own Energy Weapons** (up to its Ammo capacity) OR **Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your Room**. The normal prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors applies. To reload someone else's Weapon, Trade the Charge to them first; you cannot use it directly on their Weapon. | | Molotov Cocktail | **1; One Use Only — discard after use** | May be used in Combat | Choose your Room or a neighboring Room **containing an Intruder** (uncarried Eggs also permit the target, as under Eggs). **Place Fire** there; immediately, **each Intruder suffers 1 Injury and each Character suffers 1 Serious Wound**, including you if you are there. does the Event Phase begin automatically

requested_parts: When you use Canteen or Shower
what non-scanning benefit does each Room give
Must you choose between that benefit and scanning Contamination, or can one Room Action give both
May you take the non-scanning benefit without choosing to scan
answers.answer:
1. The summary states: - **Airlock Control** — pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors: automatically Close every Door around it and place the Airlock Procedure token there. If all those Doors are still Closed when the current Player Phase ends (all players passed), EVERYTHING in that Room dies (Characters and Intruders) and any Fire marker there is removed; if any of the Doors is opened first, the procedure is cancelled. - **Cabins** — passive: at the start of a new turn, a Character here with no Intruders present draws 1 extra Action card (hand of 6 instead of 5). Disabled by a Malfunction token. - **Canteen** — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). - **Command Center** — choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which). - **Engine Control Room** — check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here). - **Hatch Control System** — flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. - **Monitoring Room** — secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw). - **Room Covered With Slime** — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker **before resolving its Exploration token**, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). - **Shower Room** — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering. - When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it **on top of their Action discard pile**. It then cycles into their deck and hand like an Action card, but grants no Actions and cannot pay Action costs. - Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner: place the Scanner's red foil over the card's coded text field. If the exact word **INFECTED** appears in one line, the card is Infected; if it does not, the card is **not Infected**. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count.
